hypothesis: If the human stature curve has the stated shape, mean growth velocity is very high in infancy, roughly steady in childhood, peaks in the teens, and falls near zero at adulthood.
pass_criterion: Using mean measured stature by age from NHANES body measures: velocity at age 0–1 exceeds velocity at ages 4–8 by at least 2×; velocity at ages 4–8 stays within 4–8 cm/yr; the maximum velocity at ages 10–15 exceeds the ages 6–9 mean by at least 20%; and velocity after age 18 is below 1 cm/yr.
fail_criterion: Any of these conditions fails, in particular if no adolescent velocity peak exceeds the childhood mean by at least 20%, or if the childhood velocity is not between 4 and 8 cm/yr.
interpretation: Thompson's curve describes individual longitudinal growth. NHANES is cross-sectional, so velocity is estimated from differences between smoothed mean stature at successive ages, separately by sex. This blurs the individual timing of the pubertal spurt, so the peak is expected to be damped.

dataset.name: National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES)
dataset.publisher: US National Center for Health Statistics, CDC
dataset.why_it_fits: NHANES body measures files have measured standing height and recumbent length with age and sex, and survey weights. These fields give mean stature by age.
